**Visual observations:**
- Affected part: stem/branch junction
- Key features: gray-brown fuzzy/dusty sporulation covering the stem — classic "gray mold" appearance
- Surrounding leaves are wilted, brown, and collapsed
- The mold growth is dense and covers the stem in a gray powdery-fluffy mass
- No white mycelial mat at soil level (rules out Southern Blight), no water-soaked lesions typical of bacterial diseases

The gray, fuzzy sporulation on the stem is the hallmark sign of *Botrytis cinerea* (Gray Mold). This distinguishes it from powdery mildew (which appears on leaf surfaces as white powder) and from Sclerotinia (which has coarser white cottony mycelium with black sclerotia).
